comments.text_zh: 感谢你为让这篇报道得以发表所做的贡献！如果你还没看过，BBC 系列片《The Century of the Self》详细讲述了这些倾向的前史：Freud 的侄子 Edward Bernays 如何创建公关行业 [0]。它真的既引人入胜又令人恐惧——整整四五个小时都是如此！社交媒体/大数据也通过利用消费者的社交图谱数据，把消费者变成了大众成瘾的（并非完全自愿或清醒的）_生产者_。这里有一种虚构的“工作合同”：把你的数据给我，我们就给你快感。这种关系建立在无薪劳动之上。如果这种劳动——它对 BigTech 的价值——得到承认，会怎样？这就打开了大规模拒绝的可能性。从某种意义上说，人们现在使用社交媒体的方式已经由许多类型的拒绝构成，有些更有效，有些没那么有效。举一个明显的例子——Facebook 在世界各地被用作政治组织工具。这让它对镇压性政府——从美国政府开始——成为更有价值的商品，这一事实并不能阻止我们使用它并觉得它有效，也不能阻止我们在“in real life”中聚在一起。关于成瘾的社会基础，还需要说更多。这不只是广告科学家在按那些被充分研究过的生物按钮。这是生活在一个把数量多得离谱的人关起来、给自己的孩子服用精神药物、用有毒环境和有毒快餐毒害他们、把 p 分隔开的社会中的创伤
comments.text: Thanks for your part in getting this story published! If you have not seen it, the BBC series "The Century of the Self" details the pre-history of these tendencies in the creation of the public relations industry by Freud's nephew Edward Bernays [0]. It is truly fascinating and horrific -- all 4 or 5 hours of it! Social media/big data has also made the consumer a (not fully willing or conscious) _producer_ of mass addiction, through the exploitation of their social graph data. There is a fictive "work contract": give me your data and we'll give you your buzz. This relationship is based on unwaged work. What if this work, the value of it to BigTech, were recognized? It leaves open the possibility of mass refusal. And in some sense how people use social media now is already composed of many types of refusal, some more and some less effective. To state one obvious way -- Facebook is used around the world as a tool for political organizing. The fact that this makes it an even more valuable commodity for repressive governments, starting with the US government, does not stop us from using it and finding it effective, does not stop us from getting together "in real life". More needs to be said about the social basis of addiction. It's not only ad scientists pushing well-studied biological buttons. comments.text_zh: 当然，老兄。我是伴着 Apple ][ 和 C64 长大的，我们那时都看到一个未来：小企业和有创造力的人会制作古怪、信息丰富又可爱的小简报，来宣传自己的商品。我们的父母和老师为我们将要面对的世界做准备，那世界大体上就像 1980 年存在的那个世界，但像记账这样讨厌的部分被 6502 改善了。我们也上了一点网，但主要是瞎逛、交换一些软件，有时也许讨论和互喷，但它始终只是生活中极小的一部分，对我们时间的占用大概和纸牌游戏 UNO 差不多。它是有趣的消遣，但肯定不是日常活动，更谈不上依赖。当然，现在年纪大了，我们意识到幕后还酝酿着更多东西：企业一直在利用 Freud 的心理学原理把我们变成狂热的消费者。冷战偏执催生了一场军备竞赛。美国军事霸权正一路走向顶点。我们继续埋头前行，为大学里有互联网而乐在其中，但仍然找时间玩音乐、聚会、骑车等等。突然在 2000 年前后，网络化把美国生活中的军事性和商业性融合成了随身携带的 cookies 大商场。但有了这么多通信技术，为什么只在我们坐在 Pentium II 前时才用它？让每个人都随身带手机 -> 监视资本主义。当我重看 The Century of Self 时，这一切开始在我脑中串起来了：[VIDEO] 该怎么办？意见不一。许多人会争论我们能否通过立法摆脱
comments.text: Of course, man. I grew up with the Apple ][ and C64 and we all saw a future where small businesses and creative people would make zany, informative, cute newsletters to advertise their wares. Our parents and teachers prepared us for a world mostly like the one that existed in 1980, but some of the icky parts like bookkeeping were ameliorated by the 6502. We went online a little bit, but mostly to goof around, trade some software and maybe sometimes discuss and flame, but it was always a tiny part of life, about the footprint on our time as the card game UNO. An interesting diversion, but certainly not a daily activity, much less a dependency . Of course, older now, we realize there was much more brewing behind the scenes: Corporations had been leveraging Freud's psychological principles to make us rabid consumers. Cold War paranoia created an arms race. American military hegemony had been cruising to a head. We plugged on, amused we had internet in college, but still found time to play music, party, ride bikes, etc. Suddenly around 2000, networking fused the military and commercial nature of American life into the portable mega-mall of cookies. But with all this communications technology, why only use it when sitting at our Pentium II's? Let's get everyone carrying cell phones -> surveillance capitalism. comments.why_zh: 关于 Bernays 以及广告和公关历史的纪录片
comments.quote_zh: 这个帖子里的各位可能会觉得这个挺有意思：一部关于 Edward Bernays 以及广告和公关历史的四集纪录片
comments.text_zh: 这个帖子里的各位可能会觉得这个挺有意思：一部关于 Edward Bernays 以及我们今天所知的广告和公关历史的四集纪录片。[视频] 视频简介写道——“这是 Sigmund Freud 和他的美国侄子 Edward Bernays 之间关系的故事。Bernays 在 1920 年代发明了公共关系这一行业，也是第一个把 Freud 的理念用于操控大众的人。他向美国企业展示，如何通过系统性地把大批量生产的商品与人们无意识的欲望联系起来，让人们想要他们其实并不需要的东西。Bernays 是现代大众消费说服技巧的主要设计者之一，他使尽了浑身解数，从名人代言、出格的公关噱头，到把汽车情色化。他最臭名昭著的一招，是通过说服女性香烟是独立与自由的象征，打破了女性吸烟的禁忌。但 Bernays 深信，这不仅仅是推销消费品的方式。这是一种关于如何控制大众的全新政治理念。通过满足他叔叔所发现的那些内在非理性欲望，人们可以被弄得快乐，从而变得顺从。这就是那个吞噬一切的自我——如今已主导当今世界——的起点。”
comments.text: Folks in this thread may find this interesting, a 4 part documentary on Edward Bernays and the history of advertising and PR as we know it today. [VIDEO] From the video description - "The story of the relationship between Sigmund Freud and his American nephew, Edward Bernays. Bernays invented the public relations profession in the 1920s and was the first person to take Freud's ideas to manipulate the masses. He showed American corporations how they could make people want things they didn't need by systematically linking mass-produced goods to their unconscious desires. Bernays was one of the main architects of the modern techniques of mass-consumer persuasion, using every trick in the book, from celebrity endorsement and outrageous PR stunts, to eroticising the motorcar. His most notorious coup was breaking the taboo on women smoking by persuading them that cigarettes were a symbol of independence and freedom. But Bernays was convinced that this was more than just a way of selling consumer goods. It was a new political idea of how to control the masses. By satisfying the inner irrational desires that his uncle had identified, people could be made happy and thus docile. It was the start of the all-consuming self which has come to dominate today's world."

comments.text_zh: 我可以建议你读一下 David Graeber 的《The Utopia of Rules》（愿他安息）。[LINK] [LINK] 他论证说，我们已经建立了一个庞大的官僚体系，大多数工作都是 bullshit jobs（狗屁工作，这个词就是他创造的），大多数工作都是骗局。我们本可以实行 UBI，让大多数人每周只工作几个小时，但那么多自由是危险的。政客可能会失去权力。更严肃地说，去看看 Adam Curtis 的《The Century of the Self》，[LINK] [VIDEO]，它描述了 20 世纪营销作为一种社会力量的诞生与兴起；消费型社会是如何被创造出来的。这背后的一个巨大驱动力是需要“控制大众”，因为如果大众不被控制，就会发生糟糕的事情。比如世界大战或水晶之夜。Bullshit jobs 和无所不包的官僚体系——让人们一直工作、无法思考——就是我们当前控制大众的社会技术。
comments.text: May I suggest you read "The Utopia of Rules" by David Graeber (may he rest in peace). [LINK] [LINK] He argues that we've built a giant bureaucracy, most jobs are bullshit jobs (he created that term), and most work is a scam. We could have UBI and most people working just a few hours per week, but that much freedom is dangerous. Politicians might loose power. More seriously, watch The Century of the Self (Adam Curtis), [LINK] [VIDEO] , which describes the creation and rise of marketing as a social force in the 1900s; how the consumer-based society was created. A large driver of this was the need to "control the masses", because if they weren't controlled bad things happened. Like world wars or crystal nights. Bullshit jobs and an all-encompassing bureaucracy, keeping people working all the time and unable to think, is our current social technique for controlling the masses.

comments.text_zh: 企业和政府一样，都会进行无处不在的宣传，从人易受影响的求学岁月一直到成年。Edward Burnays 说，宣传在一战后声名狼藉，于是他们把它改名为“PR”。企业也是这么让女性吸烟的：[LINK] 他们如何控制人群，主角是 Edward Burnays 和他的叔叔 Freud（讽刺的是，Freud 的理论出名还是因为他这个侄子）：[VIDEO] 企业界如何向孩子营销：[LINK] 他们把它营销给黑人青年：[LINK] 他们把它营销给少女：[LINK] 有时面具会掉下来，他们做得太露骨：[LINK] 新闻公司和社交网络的营利模式，让越来越多成年人变得长期愤怒，并在政治上部落化：[LINK] 他们为了取悦股东而诉诸的东西甚至有个术语：监视资本主义：[LINK] Sheryl Sandberg 在 NYC 发布她的书《Lean In》时，我就在现场：[LINK] 别搞错了。YCombinator 和股东资本主义不可避免地会导致这种情况。企业必须永远取悦股东。而且越来越大力推动包容性，其中一部分意味着让来自传统角色的人（例如女性家庭主妇）适应那些有利于市场的工作类型。随着两性都涌入劳动力市场，工资被压低，婚姻率下降。人们被分散注意力，变成比如性别战士（Red Pill 对 Feminism），而不是意识到他们都在被一个营利性资本主义制度剥削。
comments.text: Corporations, just like governments, engage in pervasive propaganda, from impressionable school years all the way to adulthood. Edward Burnays said propaganda got a bad name after WW1, so they renamed it to "PR". It's how corporations got women to smoke, too: [LINK] How they control the crowd, featuring Edward Burnays and his uncle Freud (whose theories became famous ironically because of his nephew): [VIDEO] How the corporate world market to kids: [LINK] They marketed it to Black youth: [LINK] They marketed it to teen girls: [LINK] Sometimes the mask comes off and they do it too openly: [LINK] The for-profit model of news corporations and social networks has led more and more adults to become perpetually angry and tribal politically: [LINK] There is even a term for what they resort to in order to please shareholders: surveillance capitalism: [LINK] I was at the event in NYC when Sheryl Sandberg unveiled her book, "Lean In": [LINK] Make no mistake. YCombinator and shareholder capitalism leads to this inevitably. Corporations have to please shareholders forever. And there is more and more push for inclusivity and part of that means adapting people from traditional roles (e.g. women homemakers) into types of work that benefit the market. As both sexes flooded the labor pool, wages got depressed, and marriage declined. People are distracted into being e.g. gender warriors (Red Pill vs Feminism) rather than realizing they are all being exploited by a for-profit capitalist system

comments.why_zh: 第一集说明了 Freud 的理论如何被用来控制人群
comments.quote_zh: “这部系列片讲的是，在大众民主时代，掌权者如何利用 Freud 的理论来试图控制危险的人群。”
comments.text_zh: 广告已经如此深度地融入美国生活方式，我不知道那是否真的会发生。当权者不会放弃他们的玩具。直到大概 Google、然后是 Facebook 出现之前，这个家伙单枪匹马通过投放广告所做的事，可能比任何人都多。[LINK] > 他最著名的宣传活动包括 1929 年的一次努力：把香烟包装成女权主义的“Torches of Freedom”（自由火炬），以此推动女性吸烟；以及他在 1950 年代为 United Fruit Company 所做的工作，这与 1954 年由 CIA 策划的推翻危地马拉民选政府有关。批评者认为，他在危地马拉的参与助推了美国帝国主义，并助长了数十年的内乱与镇压，引发了关于他在破坏民主治理中所扮演角色的伦理担忧。 > 他曾为数十家美国大公司工作，包括 Procter & Gamble 和 General Electric，也为政府机构、政客和非营利组织工作。他的叔叔是精神分析师 Sigmund Freud。[LINK] > 《The Century of the Self》是电影制作者 Adam Curtis 于 2002 年推出的英国电视纪录片系列。它聚焦于精神分析师 Sigmund Freud 和 Anna Freud，以及公关顾问 Edward Bernays 的工作。在第一集中，Curtis 说：“这部系列片讲的是，在大众民主时代，掌权者如何利用 Freud 的理论来试图控制危险的人群。”[VIDEO]
comments.text: Advertising is so integrated into the American way of life, I don't know if that will ever happen. The powers-that-be won't give up their toys. This one guy single-handedly did more by running ads than anyone else until probably Google, then Facebook. [LINK] > His best-known campaigns include a 1929 effort to promote female smoking by branding cigarettes as feminist "Torches of Freedom", and his work for the United Fruit Company in the 1950s, connected with the CIA-orchestrated overthrow of the democratically elected Guatemalan government in 1954. Critics argue that his involvement in Guatemala facilitated US imperialism and contributed to decades of civil unrest and repression, raising ethical concerns about his role in undermining democratic governance. > He worked for dozens of major American corporations, including Procter & Gamble and General Electric, and for government agencies, politicians, and nonprofit organizations. His uncle was psychoanalyst Sigmund Freud. [LINK] > The Century of the Self is a 2002 British television documentary series by filmmaker Adam Curtis. It focuses on the work of psychoanalysts Sigmund Freud and Anna Freud, and PR consultant Edward Bernays. In episode one, Curtis says, "This series is about how those in power have used Freud's theories to try and control the dangerous crowd in an age of mass democracy." [VIDEO]

comments.quote_zh: 和往常一样，他为了效果而夸大了
comments.text_zh: 我最近开始看 Adam Curtis 的《Century of the Self》[1]，然后决定去查证事实 [2]。Curtis 把 Sigmund Freud 的侄子 Edward Louis Bernays 说成是现代广告的发明者，但和往常一样，他为了效果而夸大了。我长期以来一直是拆穿广告的爱好者，至少从我小时候得知自己正被心理操纵时起就是这样。我们是一个活动人士的聚集地，也是《Adbusters》杂志——一本关于心智环境的刊物——的总部。自 1989 年以来，我们这个由艺术家、设计师、作家、音乐人、诗人、朋克、哲学家和野性心灵组成的国际共同体，一直在砸广告、反腐败、向权力说真话。[3] [1] The Century of the Self - Part 1: "Happiness Machines" [VIDEO] [2] [LINK] [3] [LINK]
comments.text: I started watching Adam Curtis' Century of the Self [1] recently, then decided to fact check [2]. Curtis makes out Sigmund Freuds nephew Edward Louis Bernays as the inventor of modern advertising, but he exaggerates for effect as usual. I've been a fan of busting ads for a long time, at least since I learned as a boy that I was being psychologically manipulated. We're an activist hub and the headquarters of Adbusters magazine, the journal of the mental environment. Since 1989, our international collective of artists, designers, writers, musicians, poets, punks, philosophers and wild hearts has been smashing ads, fighting corruption and speaking truth to power.
